name: r2-geglu-die-probe-ctl
author: solx-loop
description: E2/H16 asked whether the B200's two dies make the home partition of an address usable from %smid. Probes found a real latency split: remote DRAM reads take about 994 cycles against 585 local, and the home changes every 4 KB. But the home depends on a physical 2 MB-page bit that the kernel cannot compute. With a perfect host-measured map, locality still gives nothing when the stream saturates bandwidth or at S, and any die-aware dynamic assignment costs about 1 us or more. The build gate failed,
